summary: Round 1’s core issues are substantively addressed at HEAD: v0.4 now treats `0.19×` as the canonical all-Bell-summed toy quantity, demotes the result to `[CONJ]` exploratory status, keeps β-vs-Pirandola explicitly agnostic in both the finding doc and MQ §11.0.2, matches the agnostic stance in `umr_path_beta_derivation.md`, removes the old fast-track/definitive framing, and relabels the Werner branch as a heuristic surrogate with explicit toy/non-physical caveats. However, the round still cannot pass because v0.4 introduces a new internal numeric inconsistency in the sensitivity discussion for the `Ψ±` linear-optic subcase, so there is still a correctness cleanup required before the convention handling can be considered fully stable.

issues.description: The sensitivity discussion is internally inconsistent. Section 2 says the `Ψ±` linear-optic BSM convention is `~0.13×` Pir, while §3.1 says the same convention is `≈ 2/4 × all-Bell = ~0.10×` Pir and then asserts that the sensitivity numbers are mutually consistent. This does not reopen the old `0.094×` vs `0.19×` canonical/main-claim problem, but it is a new self-contradiction inside the R2 fix document.
issues.suggestion: Reconcile the `Ψ±` sensitivity number to one supported value everywhere. If it is meant to be derived from the canonical all-Bell figure, update line 67 to match `~0.10×` (or the exact recomputed value). If `~0.13×` comes from a separate calculation, document that derivation and assumptions explicitly, then adjust §3.1 and the 'mutually consistent' statement accordingly.

round_recommendation: Fix the single remaining sensitivity-number inconsistency in `beta_G3_numerical_finding_2026-04-22.md`, then do one last internal numeric-consistency pass across §2 and §3.1. With that corrected, this round would likely be ready to pass.
